headline: strong
texts: You handled this burns module with a sound method: airway first, the right test for the right question, and fluid treated as an estimate to be adjusted. Your answers held up when the question changed form. Keep that habit of reading the stem for age, timing and setting. Your review cards below will keep it fresh at spaced intervals.
Airway first is secure. You put the primary survey ahead of the fluid sum and saw why a talking patient with soot and facial burns still needs early intubation.
The inhalation-injury test ladder is secure. You know bronchoscopy confirms airway injury, that a normal early X-ray excludes nothing, and that oximetry is blind to carboxyhaemoglobin.
Antidote pairing is secure. You separate carbon monoxide (100% oxygen) from cyanide (hydroxocobalamin) by mechanism and by clinical clue.
Burn shock and fluid choice are secure. You named it hypovolaemic and kept classic Parkland to crystalloid alone, with colloid belonging to other formulae.
Depth grading is secure. You separated reduced pain from absent pain and used blanching, texture and sensation to tell deep partial from full thickness.
TBSA estimation is secure. You hold the adult figures and switch to child proportions or Lund and Browder when the patient is a child.
Parkland arithmetic is secure. You read the qualifier word, started the clock at the burn, and deducted fluid already given before setting the rate.
Titration is secure. You treated the formula as a starting estimate, raised fluid for low urine and lowered it for high, and picked the right target for age and setting.
Topical agent pairing is secure. You matched each agent to its own property and side effect.
Curling and Marjolin are secure. You placed Curling's ulcer in the gut early after a burn and Marjolin's ulcer in an old scar as squamous cell carcinoma.
Escharotomy is secure. You asked whether the eschar is constricting, and kept both qualifiers: full thickness and circumferential with compromise.
Your Sure and Guessing taps tracked your answers well. That is useful: you know when to trust yourself and when to check. Keep using the taps honestly, since the review cards rely on them.
You skipped part of a lesson. The skipped lesson's content is untested for you, so do its review cards soon, answering cold. If they come easily, the skip was reasonable; if not, rerun that segment.

No objective needs rescue. Keep the review cards on their spaced schedule at 1, 3, 7, 21 and 60 days. When you see a burn fluid question, still read the stem for age, timing and qualifier words before computing.
